title: Exponents: The Laws of Exponents
subject: Mathematics
subtopic: Multiplying, dividing and powers of powers

scenes.heading: The Laws of Exponents
scenes.narration: Welcome to part four of our algebra series. In this lesson we learn the laws of exponents and use them to simplify expressions.

scenes.heading: What is an exponent?
bullets: In $2^5$, 2 is the base and 5 is the exponent
The exponent tells you how many times the base is a factor
scenes.narration: Two to the power five means two times two times two times two times two, which is thirty two. Two is the base, and five is the exponent. The exponent tells you how many times the base is multiplied by itself.

scenes.heading: The laws
scenes.narration: Here are the laws. When you multiply powers with the same base, add the exponents. When you divide, subtract the exponents. A power of a power: multiply the exponents. A product raised to a power: raise each factor to that power. And anything to the power zero is one, as long as the base is not zero.

scenes.heading: Multiplying: add the exponents
scenes.narration: x to the four, times x cubed. The bases are the same, so add the exponents: four plus three is seven. The answer is x to the power seven.

scenes.heading: Dividing: subtract the exponents
scenes.narration: y to the nine, divided by y to the four. Subtract the exponents: nine minus four is five. The answer is y to the power five.

scenes.heading: Power of a power
scenes.narration: m squared, all to the power five: multiply the exponents, two times five is ten, so m to the ten. Now two x cubed, all squared. Square the two to get four, and multiply the exponents three times two, to get x to the six. The answer is four x to the six.

scenes.heading: Mixed example
scenes.narration: Simplify three a to the five, times four a squared, all over six a to the four. On top, multiply the numbers, three times four is twelve, and add the exponents to get a to the seven. Now divide: twelve divided by six is two, and seven minus four gives a cubed. The answer is two a cubed.

scenes.heading: The zero exponent
scenes.narration: Five to the power zero is one. Seven x, in brackets, to the power zero, is also one. But in three x to the power zero, only the x has the exponent zero. So it is three times one, which is three.

scenes.heading: Tips
bullets: Multiply the numbers, add the exponents
Only use the laws when the bases are the same
scenes.narration: Three tips. When multiplying terms, multiply the numbers but add the exponents. Only use these laws when the bases are the same. And watch the brackets: three x to the zero is three, but three x in brackets, to the zero, is one.

activity.title: The laws of exponents
activity.instructions: Simplify. Leave answers with positive exponents.
